locator.text: Equation (B.12), p. 146, in the statement of Proposition B.2

provenance.note: machine audit: worker, gate, reviewer; not confirmed by a human

verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. Three of the four clauses are literal. U = U_* + Λ⁻¹𝔲 is `affineProfile (NaturalAxisData.U j) (1/Λ) Λ u`, with `NaturalAxisData.U j η = 4*η + j` matching (B.1) U_* = 4η + j_0, and `pullback Λ F (X,η) = F (ΛX, η)` encoding Y = ΛX. Π = Π_0 + Λ⁻¹𝓘(g²Φ²) is `ProfileFamily.Pi = affineProfile P0 (1/Λ) Λ pressure` together with `IsScaledSolution.pressure_integral : P p = ∫_0^{p.1} (a p.2)²Φ(y,p.2)²` with a = g, which is exactly 𝓘(g²Φ²) in Y. g = φ_*/C is `realAmplitude = exp(Λ·realPhase h j σ)/C`, and `realPhase h j σ x = x ∫_0^1 realGradient h j σ (t x) dt` with `realGradient h j σ x = -L·H/(H²+σ²)` = ζ_* of (B.3), so realPhase = ∫_0^η ζ_*(w)dw and exp(Λ·realPhase) = φ_* of (B.3) exactly. The rewriting: the clause φ = φ_*Φ itself is not carried in Lean in that form; Lean's angular unknown is the C-normalized profile, `angularProfile (realAmplitude …) Λ phi = g·Φ = φ/C`, so the paper's φ = φ_*Φ is recovered by multiplying Lean's f by C. That this is the intended normalization is corroborated independently inside the same structure: `IsNaturalSolution.pressure_equation : partialY Pr p = (f p)^2` against the paper's (B.15) Π_X = φ²/C². The paper's 𝓘 is defined in unscaled-to-Y form on p.145; Lean integrates in the first (scaled radial) variable over [0, p.1], the same integral.
